extracted.intended_audience: scholars, psychologists, literary critics, and writers interested in the theory and production of wit/humor
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic and prescriptive criteria for identifying, explaining, and producing wit (wordplay, repartee, caricature, etc.) grounded in psychoanalytic/literary theory; focuses on verbal technique, mechanisms like condensation, and aesthetic effects such as brevity and surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as playful judgment / aesthetic freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is characterized as a 'playful judgment' arising from an æsthetic attitude of freedom—expecting nothing from the object and enjoying the play of ideas freed from conventional restrictions and rules of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lipps: wit = 'playful judgment.' Jean Paul: 'Freedom begets wit and wit begets freedom.' Produce a disposition of playful contemplation (not serious instrumental aims) when creating wit; avoid didactic or overly purposeful framing that removes the playful attitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective/active nature of wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is 'the subjective side of the comic'—the part we ourselves create, an activity of the subject (the wit-maker) rather than a passive objectified comic element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lipps: wit colors our conduct; the relation is that of 'Superior Subject.' Emphasize the agentive, creative stance in producing wit (inventive framing, active reframing) rather than relying solely on external situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity as essential (but special) characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity is traditionally held to be the body and soul of wit, but not all brevity is witty; wit's brevity is of a special kind—it 'says what it does say, not always in few, but always in too few words' and can 'leave the thing unsaid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for terseness that implies a larger suppressed thought; brevity that truncates a fuller (explicit) phrasing so the omitted material must be reconstructed by the listener/reader. Avoid mere laconism that lacks implicit reconstruction or suppressed by-thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union of dissimilarities / finding hidden similarities
rubrics_metrics.description: A traditional definition: wit is the ability to discover similarities in dissimilarities (to unite ideas that are foreign to each other quickly and unexpectedly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct juxtapositions or links between conceptually distant domains so the audience recognizes an unexpected similarity. Beware of forced or opaque analogies that cannot be immediately parsed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast of ideas / antithesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit often involves the voluntary combination or linking of two contrasted ideas—contrast may be between meanings, senses of words, or expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use antithesis or semantic contradiction to produce a sudden shift in interpretation. Ensure the contrast is perceivable and resolvable by the audience; avoid contrasts that produce confusion without resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense-in-nonsense / temporary ascription and retraction of meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit can operate by lending a meaning to an expression (psychological necessity), then immediately retracting it—producing the comic through the transition from borrowed conviction to awareness of nullity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design expressions that momentarily read as logical or senseful, then reveal that this sense was misplaced. The audience should experience an immediate volte-face from conviction to the realization of incongruity; avoid outcomes where the retraction is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession of confusion and clearness (enigmatic setup then solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A common mechanism: an initially confusing or enigmatic expression induces puzzlement, and the subsequent elucidation or reinterpretation produces the comic effect (e.g., Heine's 'famillionaire').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage the utterance so that initial parsing yields confusion; follow with immediate reinterpretation or reveal that resolves the puzzle. The timing (brevity between confusion and clarity) is crucial—delayed resolution weakens the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit unearths the hidden or suppressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit often 'unearths something hidden and concealed'—it exposes a suppressed thought or by-thought that was latent in ordinary expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the witty utterance to make the suppressed content reconstructable (through cues, fused forms, or contrasts). Avoid making the suppressed element so obscure that it cannot be recovered by the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit's effect often depends on verbal/form technique rather than thought content
rubrics_metrics.description: The witty character frequently adheres to the form of expression (wording, word-formation, phonetic play), not to the propositional thought itself; accurate paraphrase often removes the wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize linguistic form — neologisms, compressions, phonetic shifts, puns — when crafting wit. Test paraphrases: if a literal restatement removes the laugh, the form (not the bare thought) carries the wit. Avoid relying solely on propositional cleverness without distinctive form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation with substitutive formation (blend/neologism formation)
rubrics_metrics.description: One technique: condensation that fuses two words/meanings into a mixed/neologistic word (e.g., 'famillionaire', 'kleptorumania', 'anecdotage'), carrying both constituent senses and prompting reconstruction of omitted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form fused words that transparently evoke their parent terms so listeners can reconstruct the omitted clause or suppressed thought. Ensure the blend preserves enough of both sources to be decoded; avoid blends that are opaque or impossible to parse in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation with modification/substitution (slight modifications conveying suppressed thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Another technique: small modifications (letter change, reversal, preposition swap) in an ordinary phrase signal an omitted or suppressed idea (e.g., 'tête-à-bête' modified to imply 'bête'; 'great future behind him' replacing 'before').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply minimal, often almost imperceptible, changes to familiar expressions so that the listener infers the suppressed meaning. The smaller the modification that still communicates the suppressed thought, the stronger the wit. Avoid overly heavy-handed edits that make the transform obvious and blunt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression / abbreviation that leaves reconstructable residue
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit frequently compresses a full two-sentence thought into a single truncated utterance, leaving an element (word or syllable) that serves as a residue enabling reconstruction of the omitted part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress multi-part reasoning into a single compact expression that still contains a recoverable trace (morpheme, syllable, cue) of the omitted clause. The audience must be able to 'fill in' the compressed content; don't omit so much that there is no clue for reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification by technical means and utilization in speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit can be categorized by technical means (sound-wit, play on words, caricature, characterization wit, witty repartee) and by how it is used in discourse (repartee versus elaborated epigram).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing wit, identify which technical class the example falls into and apply class-specific expectations (e.g., repartee expects quickness and interpersonal timing; play-on-words expects phonetic or semantic double-readings). Use appropriate delivery and context for each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy to dream-work condensation (latent→manifest transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The condensation observed in wit is analogous to the dream-work's condensation: latent thoughts are compressed into manifest expressions by similar psychic processes, yielding fused images/words that require interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use psychoanalytic insight: consider that witty compressions often mask underlying latent thoughts (motives, forbidden content). For deeper analysis of a witticism, attempt to reconstruct latent by-thoughts as one would in dream interpretation. For production, leverage this mechanism to hint at suppressed material for added depth.
